I am wondering if anyone here has ever used this method and perhaps can share advice or links? I have been researching on the topic and have been seeing a lot of conflicting material, so I figure I would ask you guys.
Making cannabutter using a pressure cooker?

I've been paying attention to this for a while, and as you've seen, the quality of information available on the internet varies quite a bit.

Some people grow their own, and they have tons of trim left over. They will develop techniques that work well for them, which are good for easily getting something useful out of a large quantity of low-grade material. But when some guy at home with two grams of bud tries to make something, he's going to really notice it if the process isn't efficient.

There are two separate issues - the first is decarbing, which requires a certain window of time and temperature, and the second is separation, where the useful substances (including, but not limited to THC) are separated from the plant matter.

A slow cooker with butter in it is going to to a great job of separation, the only issue is how well it does the decarbing. You can do some or all of the decarbing before slow-cooking, and adjust the times accordingly.

So what times and temperatures should you use? Great question. There are various numbers suggested, and a few actual experiments where decarbing is measured, but it can be hard to reproduce these same conditions at home. Putting some ground bud in a covered dish in a 300F oven for twenty minutes does not mean the bud itself actually got to 300F for that length of time.

The best you can do is to decide on a technique that is convenient and repeatable, and just try it a few times, varying the times and temperatures until you find what works. Here's my technique, which works well but I think there is still room for improvement:
